verses.1: On the first day of the week, at dawn, they went to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.
verses.2: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
verses.3: Entering, they did not find the body.
verses.4: Just as they were wondering about this, two men in shining garments appeared beside them.
verses.5: In great fear, they bowed their faces to the ground. The men said to them, "Why are you looking for the living among the dead?
verses.6: He is not here, but he has risen. Remember how he told you while still in Galilee,
verses.7: saying, 'The Son of Man must be handed over to the hands of sinners and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.'"
verses.9: Returning from the tomb, they told all these things to the eleven apostles and the rest.
verses.10: It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the others with them who told the apostles.
verses.11: But their words seemed like nonsense to the apostles, and they did not believe them.
verses.12: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. He stooped to look in and saw only the linen cloths. Then he went home, amazed at what had happened.
verses.13: Now behold, two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seventy stades from Jerusalem,
verses.14: and they were talking with one another about all these events.
verses.15: And as they talked and debated, Jesus himself came up and walked with them,
verses.16: but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
verses.17: He said to them, "What are these words you are exchanging with each other as you walk?" They stood still, looking sad.
verses.18: One of them, named Cleopas, answered, "Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem and have you not known the things that have happened there in these days?"
verses.19: He said to them, "What things?" They replied, "The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
verses.20: how the chief priests and our rulers handed him over to be condemned to death, and they crucified him.
verses.21: We had hoped that he was the one who would redeem Israel. But in addition to all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
verses.22: Also, certain women from our group have astonished us. They went to the tomb at dawn,
verses.23: and did not find his body. Instead, they came back saying they had seen a vision from angels who said he is alive.
verses.24: Some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him."
verses.25: Then he said to them, "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
verses.26: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?"
verses.27: Then beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
verses.28: When they came near the village to which they were going, he made as if to go on further.
verses.29: But they urged him, saying, "Stay with us, for it is toward evening, and the day is already leaning." And he went in to stay with them.
verses.30: Now when he was at the table with them, he took the bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them.
verses.31: Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized him. And he vanished from their sight.
verses.32: They said to each other, "Was not our heart burning within us while he was talking with us on the road and explaining the scriptures to us?"
verses.33: Then they got up at that hour and returned to Jerusalem. There they found the eleven gathered together with those with them,
verses.34: saying, "Indeed, the Lord has risen and appeared to Simon."
verses.35: And the two were telling what had happened on the road and how he had been recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.
verses.36: While they were still speaking, he himself stood among them.
verses.37: They were startled and terrified, thinking they were seeing a ghost.
verses.38: He said to them, "Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
verses.39: Look at my hands and my feet. It is I myself. Touch me and see. A ghost does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have."
verses.40: And saying this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
verses.41: But while they were still disbelieving for joy and marveling, he said to them, "Do you have anything here to eat?"
verses.42: They gave him a piece of broiled fish,
verses.43: and he took it and ate in front of them.
verses.44: Then he said to them, "These are my words, which I spoke to you while still with you, that everything written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled."
verses.45: Then he opened their minds to understand the scriptures,
verses.46: and he said to them, "Thus it is written that the Christ must suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
verses.47: and that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in his name to all the nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
verses.48: You are witnesses of these things.
verses.49: And behold, I send upon you what my Father promised. But stay in the city until you are clothed from above with power."
verses.50: Then he led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands, he blessed them.
verses.51: And while he was blessing them, he was parted from them and taken up into heaven.
verses.52: They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
verses.53: and they were continually in the temple praising God.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 51: The phrase "καὶ ἀνεφέρετο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν" is omitted in many modern critical editions, likely a later addition. The translation assumes its presence based on traditional readings.  
- v. 52: The phrase "προσκυνήσαντες αὐτὸν" is also omitted in some critical texts and added here as per traditional readings.

[1] On the first day of the week, at dawn, they went to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.
[2] They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
[3] Entering, they did not find the body.
[4] Just as they were wondering about this, two men in shining garments appeared beside them.
[5] In great fear, they bowed their faces to the ground. The men said to them, "Why are you looking for the living among the dead?
[6] He is not here, but he has risen. Remember how he told you while still in Galilee,
[7] saying, 'The Son of Man must be handed over to the hands of sinners and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.'"
[8] Then they remembered his words.
[9] Returning from the tomb, they told all these things to the eleven apostles and the rest.
[10] It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the others with them who told the apostles.
[11] But their words seemed like nonsense to the apostles, and they did not believe them.
[12] But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. He stooped to look in and saw only the linen cloths. Then he went home, amazed at what had happened.
[13] Now behold, two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seventy stades from Jerusalem,
[14] and they were talking with one another about all these events.
[15] And as they talked and debated, Jesus himself came up and walked with them,
[16] but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
[17] He said to them, "What are these words you are exchanging with each other as you walk?" They stood still, looking sad.
[18] One of them, named Cleopas, answered, "Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem and have you not known the things that have happened there in these days?"
[19] He said to them, "What things?" They replied, "The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
[20] how the chief priests and our rulers handed him over to be condemned to death, and they crucified him.
[21] We had hoped that he was the one who would redeem Israel. But in addition to all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
[22] Also, certain women from our group have astonished us. They went to the tomb at dawn,
[23] and did not find his body. Instead, they came back saying they had seen a vision from angels who said he is alive.
[24] Some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him."
[25] Then he said to them, "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
[26] Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?"
[27] Then beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
[28] When they came near the village to which they were going, he made as if to go on further.
[29] But they urged him, saying, "Stay with us, for it is toward evening, and the day is already leaning." And he went in to stay with them.
[30] Now when he was at the table with them, he took the bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them.
[31] Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized him. And he vanished from their sight.
[32] They said to each other, "Was not our heart burning within us while he was talking with us on the road and explaining the scriptures to us?"
[33] Then they got up at that hour and returned to Jerusalem. There they found the eleven gathered together with those with them,
[34] saying, "Indeed, the Lord has risen and appeared to Simon."
[35] And the two were telling what had happened on the road and how he had been recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.
[36] While they were still speaking, he himself stood among them.
[37] They were startled and terrified, thinking they were seeing a ghost.
[38] He said to them, "Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
[39] Look at my hands and my feet. It is I myself. Touch me and see. A ghost does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have."
[40] And saying this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
[41] But while they were still disbelieving for joy and marveling, he said to them, "Do you have anything here to eat?"
[42] They gave him a piece of broiled fish,
[43] and he took it and ate in front of them.
[44] Then he said to them, "These are my words, which I spoke to you while still with you, that everything written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled."
[45] Then he opened their minds to understand the scriptures,
[46] and he said to them, "Thus it is written that the Christ must suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
[47] and that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in his name to all the nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
[48] You are witnesses of these things.
[49] And behold, I send upon you what my Father promised. But stay in the city until you are clothed from above with power."
[50] Then he led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands, he blessed them.
[51] And while he was blessing them, he was parted from them and taken up into heaven.
[52] They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
[53] and they were continually in the temple praising God.
